messages:
Alex: Heads up — last 2 hours we've had ~40 scale-downs in eu-west that immediately triggered scale-ups again. Looks like nodes go NotReady for 30-90s then come back. Autoscaler is killing them in the interim.
Maria: ugh. that's the classic network flap pattern. which flags are we using?
Jie: current flags in prod: `--expander=random`, `--scale-down-unneeded-time=5m`, `--scale-down-unready-time=2m`, `--max-empty-bulk-delete=10`.
Tom: so we have short windows. If a node flips NotReady for ~60s it can become eligible for scale-down because unready time is only 2m and unneeded time 5m? combined math makes it fragile.
Alex: infra-bot reported a spike of `kubelet` connection resets around 10:06 and 10:28 from a handful of hosts. Likely transient network hiccup in the AZ.
Maria: we should be conservative in eu-west until network team confirms. Quick mitigations: bump `--scale-down-unready-time` to 10m, `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 10m, switch expander to `least-waste`?
Jie: least-waste helps packing but won't stop thrash if scale-down thresholds are tight. I think `--unremovable-node-recheck-time` is also relevant (we set to 1m). Increase to 10m for now.
Tom: what about `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage` and `--skip-nodes-with-system-pods` — do we have those enabled?
Alex: `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true` and `--skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false` right now. If we set `--skip-nodes-with-system-pods=true` it'll avoid removing nodes running critical infra (but we need to watch utilization impact).
Maria: Agreed. Also add a guard: annotate nodepools with priorities and use `expander=priority` with nodeGroupPriorityConfig to prefer stable reserved pools for critical pods.
Jie: note on spot mixing — many of the removed nodes were spot. We can lower spot percentage in auto-provisioning for this region or give spots a longer grace (taint with `spot=true` and set expander to avoid evicting non-spot first).
Tom: From a measurable perspective: set `--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.25` (current 0.1) and `--scale-down-candidates-pool-min-count=50`? Not sure on that second one.
Alex: candidates pool param is a newer flag on our autoscaler build, it's currently default. Let's not tweak too many at once. Proposed roll: 
- `--scale-down-unready-time=10m`
- `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m`
- `--unremovable-node-recheck-time=10m`
- `--skip-nodes-with-system-pods=true`
- temporary `--expander=least-waste` in eu-west
Maria: +1 to staged rollout. Do we want to patch only eu-west nodepools? we can run a flag override on the autoscaler deployment with a kubeconfig context restricted to eu-west cluster.
Jie: yes patch eu-west first. Also increase `--nodes-min-count` for gpu-pools to avoid complete empty-out during the flap window (set to current min+1).
Tom: any downstream impacts to rollout speeds? least-waste will try to pack which might increase preemption in some nodepools with taints. We'll monitor.
Alex: infra-bot: creating a rollbackable k8s patch for the autoscaler in eu-west with above flags.
infra-bot: Patch draft created: `deploy/autoscaler/eu-west/autoscaler-deploy-2027-09-14.yml` (see internal link) :white_check_mark:
Maria: good. Also ask networking to run packet capture / interface counters on the affected AZ for the last 3 incidents. If it's flapping physical link we need an SRE ticket.
Jie: note: add a Prometheus alert for `autoscaler.scale_down.thrash_rate > 5/min` to detect repeated scale-down+up cycles.
Tom: and add a KPI on P95 pod startup latency to ensure increasing thresholds don't hide regressions.
Alex: rolling this in now to eu-west canary at 11:20. will post results.
Maria: thanks. If we still see thrash after 30m revert and we'll try longer `unneeded` windows or reduce spot mix. :+1:
Alex: update 11:45 — canary looks stable so far, zero repeated scale-ups for the patched pools. will continue to monitor for 1h.
Jie: nice. tagging `@networking-team` to follow up with traces.
Tom: reminder to update runbook SOP: example thresholds and which flags to tune for transient network flaps. current doc needs an eu-west note.
Alex: will PR runbook after monitoring window. thanks everyone.
